questions.question: Which of the following bacteria grow in milk and convert it to curd?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lactobacilus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lactobacilus** are responsible for the **fermentation **process that converts **milk into curd**.
 
• These bacteria produce lactic acid as a byproduct of lactose fermentation, which lowers the pH of milk, causing it to coagulate and form curd.
 
• Common types of lactic acid bacteria involved in this process include **Lactobacillus bulgaricus** and **Streptococcus thermophilus**.
 
• The production of curd is a traditional method of preserving milk and enhancing its nutritional value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Curd is a rich source of **probiotics**, which are beneficial bacteria that aid in digestion and improve gut health.
 
• It also contains essential nutrients like **calcium, protein, and vitamins**, making it a valuable addition to the diet.
 
• In many cultures, curd is used in a variety of dishes and is a staple in traditional cuisine.
 
• The fermentation process not only enhances the flavor of milk but also extends its shelf life.

questions.question: Which of the following are NOT antimicrobial drugs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Antacids.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs.

 
 
• Antacids are not antimicrobial drugs. Instead, they are medications that neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve symptoms of indigestion, heartburn, or acid reflux.
 
• They do not directly target microorganisms but rather work on the acidity level in the stomach.
 
• Common antacids include substances like calcium carbonate, magnesium hydroxide, and aluminum hydroxide.
 
 
 
• **Antibiotics -** 
 
 
• Antibiotics are antimicrobial drugs that specifically target and kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria.
 
• They are used to treat bacterial infections and work by interfering with bacterial processes, such as cell wall synthesis or protein production.
 
• Examples include penicillin, tetracycline, and amoxicillin.
 
 
 
• **​****Antiseptics **- 
 
 
• ​Antiseptics are substances applied to living tissues, such as skin, to reduce the risk of infection.
 
• Unlike disinfectants, antiseptics are safe for use on living tissues and are used to clean wounds, cuts, and surgical sites.
 
• Examples include iodine, hydrogen peroxide, and rubbing alcohol.
 
 
 
• **Disinfectants** - 
 
 
• ​Disinfectants are chemical substances used to eliminate or reduce the number of microorganisms on surfaces and inanimate objects.
 
• They are not typically used on living tissues but are effective against bacteria, viruses, and fungi.
 
• Common disinfectants include bleach, hydrogen peroxide, and alcohol-based solutions.

questions.question: Fishes have ________ chambers of the heart.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **heart **of a **fish **has **two chambers**.
 
• There is only** one ventricle** and **one atrium** in the heart.
 
• The ventricle is in charge of pumping blood into the atrium.
 
• Fish likewise have** unidirectional flow**, or a **single circulation** in a single direction.
 
• A** fish’s heart is also known as** a **venous heart** because it is filled with deoxygenated blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Number of chambers of the heart in different species:
 
• 
 
 
 

 **Species**
 **Chamber of heart**
 
 

 Mammal (including Humans) and Bird (Aves)
 four-chambered (two artria, two ventricles)
 
 

 Reptile and Dinosaur, Amphibian (including frogs and toads)
 three chambers, two atria and one ventricle (exception is crocodile with four chambers)
 
 

 Fish and Insect 
 two chambers, an atrium and a ventricle

questions.question: Snails is an example of which of the phylum of animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mollusca**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mollusca:-**

 
 
• **Molluscs are characterized by their soft bodies, which are often protected by a hard shell. **
 
• They also have a unique digestive system that includes a muscular foot, a radula (a tongue-like organ with rows of teeth), and a gizzard. 
 
• Molluscs are divided into several classes, including the Gastropoda (snails and slugs), Bivalvia (clams and oysters), Cephalopoda (squids, octopuses, and nautiluses), and Polyplacophora (chitons).
 
• **Snails are an example of the phylum Mollusca.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropoda:-**

 
 
• **It is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, comprising about 80% of all known animal species. **
 
• Arthropods live in all habitats on Earth, from the sea to the air, and from the poles to the tropics.
 
 
 
• **Protochordates:-**
 
 
• **These are an informal category of animals that are closely related to vertebrates. **
 
• They are invertebrates, but they share many of the same characteristics as vertebrates, such as a notochord (a flexible rod that runs along the back of the animal), a dorsal nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits.
 
 
 
• **Annelida:-**
 
 
• **It is a phylum of segmented worms, with over 22,000 extant species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches. **
 
• The species exist in and have adapted to various ecologies – some in marine environments as distinct as tidal zones and hydrothermal vents, others in fresh water, and yet others in moist terrestrial environments.

questions.question: Mosquito belongs to ________ phylum of the animal kingdom.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropoda.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosquito **belongs to the **phylum Arthropoda** in the animal kingdom.
 
• The Arthropoda phylum includes **insects, spiders, crustaceans**, and other arthropods. 
 
• **Arthropods are characterized by their jointed appendages and exoskeletons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mosquitoes** are further classified as members of the family Culicidae within the order Diptera, which also includes flies.
 
• **Ctenophora is a phylum of marine animals commonly known as comb jellies.**
 
• **Chordata is a phylum that includes animals with spinal cords such as mammals and fish.**
 
• **Mollusca **is a phylum of animals that includes **snails, clams, and octopuses.**

questions.question: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lemon.​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Lemons contain about 31 grams of Vitamin C.
 
• It is also known as ascorbic acid and is found in citrus fruits (like orange, and lemon), kiwifruit, guava, broccoli, strawberries, etc. 
 
• It is an essential nutrient and is not synthesized by the human body. It is a water-soluble vitamin.
 
• Functions - Repair of tissues, acts as a co-factor in many enzymatic reactions, important for the Immune system, acts as an antioxidant.
 
• C6H8O6 is the chemical formula of Vitamin C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is on the List of Essential Medicines of the World Health Organization.
 
• Deficiency Disease - The deficiency of Vitamin C causes scurvy. 
 
• Discovery - It was discovered in 1912 and first isolated in 1928.

questions.question: Which of the following is a warm blooded animal?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Ape**__ is a warm-blooded animal.
 
• Warm-blooded animals are those which can make their own body heat. Birds and mammals are warm-blooded.
 
• Cold-blooded animals are those whose body temperature depends on the temperature outside.
 
• Fish, reptiles, and amphibians are all cold-blooded.

 
 

 **Warm-blooded**
 **Cold-blooded**
 
 

 **Apes**
 Turtle
 
 

 Monkeys
 Snake
 
 

 Cat
 Fish
 
 

 Mice
 Frogs
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Thermoregulation

 
 
• Thermoregulation is the ability of an organism to maintain a core body temperature, which is 37° C (98°F) within an optimal physiological range.
 
• The hypothalamus, a portion of the brain which plays an important role in regulating body temperature by acting as a thermostat.
 
• Thermoregulation is also called heat regulation.
 
 
 
• Ectothermic Animals
 
 
• They are commonly called cold-blooded animals.
 
• They gain most of their heat from external sources.
 
• They produce a very less amount of heat to keep their body warm and have a low metabolic rate. Examples of ectothermic animals include amphibians, fish, lizards, other reptiles, etc.
 
 
 
• Endothermic Animals
 
 
• They are commonly called warm-blooded animals.
 
• They develop most of the heat mainly from their body’s metabolisms and produce a required amount of heat to keep their body warm.
 
• These animals have a very high metabolic rate.
 
• Examples of Endothermic animals include all mammals and birds.

questions.question: Whittaker classified organisims into how many kingdoms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __5__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Biologists, such as **Ernst Haeckel (1894)**, **Robert Whittaker (1969),** and** Carl Woese** (1977) have tried to classify all living organisms into broad categories, called kingdoms.
 
• The classification Whittaker proposed has **5 kingdoms**__: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
 
• His five-kingdom classification of organisms is widely used.
 
• These groups are formed on the basis of their cell structure, mode and source of nutrition and body organization.

 
• The five-kingdom classification was given by RH Whittaker in the year 1969.
 
• He mainly classified the organisms based on several characteristics like -
 
 
• Mode of nutrition
 
• Thallus organization
 
• Cell structure
 
• Phylogenetic relationship
 
• Reproduction
 
 
 
• According to the classification, the living organisms can be divided into 5 kingdoms-
 
 
• Monera- Includes all the prokaryotes
 
• Protista- Includes all the unicellular eukaryotes
 
• Fungi- includes all the fungal organisms
 
• Plantae- includes all the plants
 
• Animalia- includes all the multicellular animals
